chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Studies at Western and learning to read from Jack Washington
summary: Electrical engineering, then a printing certificate; Jack Washington taught him to read music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What were you studying in this college?

I went there to study electrical engineering. But after the first year, it was disqualified; the school lost its credit rating. And so I went in and I thought I was going into a journalism course, and ended up getting a certificate in printing. I learned how--I know how to do, to run a printing press. (chuckle)
No, I did a little commercial work on the print press, but I didn't --you know, like--get a chance to write anything.
You weren't studying music then, here?

No, I didn't. I took up a course there with Marie Little, when she took over the thing on a band, in music arranging and public school music and all that stuff. But most of it I had already learned, 'cause Jack Washington was a graduate of Western University.
Oh, the saxophone player. Little Jack.

Yeah. I used to go over to his house, and he'd show me everything about reading. That's how I learned how to read, from Jack. But I took a course in public school music and like that. And this was what you'd say--what you'd teach in the elementary grades, you know, the fundamentals of music. Write a line of melody notes; then you'd find out what chords you'd put with it. Then you'd find out what your signature is like. Very elementary, music.
